html:
The Taif Agreement was the deal that ended the Lebanese Civil War. Lebanese members of parliament agreed on it in October 1989 at Taif in Saudi Arabia.

It kept the sharing of power by religion but changed the balance. Seats in parliament were split equally between Christians and Muslims, instead of six to five in the Christians' favour. Much of the power of the Maronite president passed to the cabinet and its Sunni prime minister. All militias were to disarm.

Fighting ended in 1990. In practice Syria kept its army in Lebanon until 2005, and Hezbollah kept its weapons as a resistance against Israel. The agreement is still the basis of Lebanon's constitution. See also National Pact.
sum: The Taif Agreement was the deal that ended the Lebanese Civil War. Lebanese members of parliament agreed on it in October 1989 at Taif in Saudi Arabia.
